description: Lightweight index for workbench historical session records.

entries.title: browser-harness thin browser substrate case study and web-based intake
entries.summary: Attempted to clone browser-harness to D:\browser-harness but GitHub connectivity to github.com:443 failed, so the case was archived through GitHub web analysis instead. The workbench now records browser-harness as a thin CDP-first browser execution substrate case with reusable lessons around interaction-vs-domain skill separation, editable helper growth, and verification after browser side effects.
skill_promotions: Expanded case-advice metadata so browser-control, CDP, harness, and interaction-vs-domain skill questions can retrieve this case more directly
doc_promotions: Added browser-harness as a first-class thin browser substrate case in the shared case library index

followup_actions.action: Retry a local clone and perform a source-code-deep pass when GitHub connectivity to github.com:443 is available again
followup_actions.notes: The current archive is good enough for design borrowing, but a later code-level pass would strengthen implementation-specific lessons.

promotion_review.decision: This case did not justify a new stable memory rule or a direct skill-body rewrite, but it did justify archiving browser-harness as a first-class thin browser substrate reference and extending case-advice metadata so future browser-harness questions can retrieve it with clearer evidence.

entries.title: awesome-ai-research-writing knowledge-asset case study and workbench intake
entries.summary: Cloned awesome-ai-research-writing to D:\awesome-ai-research-writing, analyzed it as a research-writing prompt and skill knowledge asset rather than a runtime Agent system, added case docs plus a workbench borrowing note, and expanded the workbench to treat knowledge-product repositories as first-class reference cases.
skill_promotions: Added a dedicated research-writing task router that maps natural-language writing requests to prompt and skill paths
doc_promotions: Added awesome-ai-research-writing as a first-class knowledge-asset case in the shared case library index

followup_actions.action: Consider adding a dedicated knowledge-asset routing template if more prompt-library and skill-onboarding repositories are archived
followup_actions.notes: One case is enough to justify the category, but not yet enough to finalize a richer reusable template.

promotion_review.decision: This case mainly expanded the reusable documentation and routing coverage of the case library. It did not require a new stable memory rule or a direct skill-body rewrite, but it did justify explicit case-library and advisor updates for knowledge-asset style repositories.

entries.title: Initial Hermes Agent case study and workbench borrowing analysis
entries.summary: Cloned Hermes Agent to D:\hermes-agent, analyzed it as a long-running and memory-first agent workbench, added user and agent case docs, added comparison docs against deer-flow and claude-code, and extracted the most valuable ideas for upgrading the current workbench.
skill_promotions: Promoted Hermes-derived workbench lessons into autonomous-delivery-default and the 4 core Agent research skills
memory_promotions: Promoted stable workbench rule that new information should enter sessions first
Promoted stable autonomous execution preference with phase reporting and evidence tracking
doc_promotions: Created shared development phase report template
Added workbench development report to track implementation phases

followup_actions.action: Continue connecting session workflow to skill and memory feedback checks
followup_actions.notes: The workflow now records promotions, but future sessions still need stronger default checks and automation.

promotion_review.decision: This session promoted reusable methods into skills, durable rules into memory, and shared artifacts into docs, so all three promotion paths were explicitly checked and recorded.
